overview: This Senate resolution honors the life of John Bennett Johnston Jr., who represented Louisiana in the U.S. Senate from 1972 to 1997 and died at age 92. It recounts his service as an Army lawyer, his time in the Louisiana legislature, and his years chairing the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, where he shaped national energy policy. It highlights his work on flood control, wetland preservation, offshore drilling, and creating national parks in Louisiana. The resolution expresses the Senate's sorrow, sends a copy to his family, and adjourns the Senate in his memory. The Senate agreed to it on April 7, 2025.
for: Supporters say it is a fitting tribute to a long-serving senator whose work on energy and conservation had lasting effects on Louisiana and the country.
against: Critics say it is a symbolic gesture that does not change any law or spending.
